summary: With viewContext on (the default), createAiChatHandler sends <view-context and </view-context in the text of user messages to the model as <view-context (ASCII spelling and its listed variants). Text without the name view-context is byte-identical.
howTo: Nothing to do. Only the model input changes, and only for user text that contains the name view-context: there for every tag the pattern matches (any case, whitespace, zero-width characters or a soft hyphen between < and the name or around the /, <view-context-…>; a typed < before the name becomes &lt;; in such text also a < before 64 or more whitespace or zero-width characters). The chat, the stream, the PII shield, the guardrails and a custom streamHandler still get the text as the user wrote it. Not caught: full-width or look-alike characters (＜, homoglyphs, other hyphens), a line break or invisible character inside the name, entities such as <, a tag split across text parts or messages, the content of file attachments (their placeholder text carries the file name, so a file name with the tag is escaped), tool call arguments of an approval continuation, the imitated header without tags, chat memory notes and summaries, tool results and assistant text. Messages the SDK writes itself (seen-objects memo, chat memory, view context block, budget continuation, final summary instruction) are never escaped. The block grants no permission either way: the server checks types, ids and facts on its own. With viewContext: false (and in the runtime container) nothing changes. Tests that assert the exact model input for user text containing <view-context need the escaped form.
